paragraphs: (Karmi son of Zavdi, Joshua, beginning of chapter 7.) Rabbi Abba bar Zavda: [Berakhot 11a](https://www.sefaria.org/Berakhot.11a.10); in [Yerushalmi Yevamot 1:6](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Yevamot.1.6.2), Rabbah bar Zavda, where Hyman interprets “Rabbah” as a compression of Rabbi Ba. Oshaya bar Zavda: [Taanit 26b](https://www.sefaria.org/Taanit.26b.17). Rabbi Bizna bar Zavda: [Berakhot 55b](https://www.sefaria.org/Berakhot.55b.16). Rabbi Yehudah bar Zavda (or Zevida): [Berakhot 12b](https://www.sefaria.org/Berakhot.12b.14). Rabbi Yaakov bar Zavdi: [Kiddushin 33b](https://www.sefaria.org/Kiddushin.33b.13). Rav Nachman bar Zavda: [Shabbat 25b](https://www.sefaria.org/Shabbat.25b.3).[^2]

notes.text: Hyman’s abbreviation claim concerns רבה alone as a compression of Rabbi Ba, not the entire patronymic. The Yevamot 1:6 reference is Jerusalem Talmud.

The linked Yerushalmi reads Rava bar Zavda. Hyman supplies Rabbah and interprets that form as Rabbi Ba. The Shabbat passage includes the fuller patronymic son of Rav Zavda and an alternative attribution to Rav Nachman bar Rava in Rav’s name.
